headline_marked: [[Qualcomm to cut jobs globally]] in 'performance-based' layoffs, pivoting to AI
headline: Qualcomm to cut jobs globally in 'performance-based' layoffs, pivoting to AI
summary: Qualcomm will begin informing affected employees in November, citing a 'performance-focused reduction' as it strategically pivots towards AI infrastructure and edge computing markets.
details: Qualcomm has announced it will cut jobs worldwide following its annual performance reviews, with notifications expected to begin in November. CEO Cristiano Amon described the move as a 'performance-focused reduction' aimed at fostering a stronger performance culture within the company.

The company, a major smartphone chip manufacturer, has been affected by an industry-wide decline in consumer electronics sales and rising memory costs. Its shares have significantly underperformed the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.

In response, Qualcomm is strategically pivoting towards AI infrastructure and edge computing, a growing trend across the semiconductor industry. The company previously unveiled its AI200 and AI250 AI inference accelerators in October 2025.

This reduction aims to optimize the workforce, allowing Qualcomm to retain valuable employees in new growth areas such as data center silicon, automotive platforms, personal computing, and edge computing, while addressing duplicated or lower-performing roles.

Amon stated the company needs 'the right people in the right roles' to succeed. The decision follows Q3 2026 financial results showing a 4% year-on-year revenue decline and a 25% lower net income, with the core handset business down 20%.

Qualcomm's layoffs reflect a broader industry trend where tech companies are trimming workforces to fund ambitious AI initiatives. Companies like Meta have also announced job cuts to invest in AI infrastructure, intensifying the competition for specialized AI talent.

headline_marked: [[AI Agents Finally Got Reliable]] in 2026 With New "Harness" Engineering
headline: AI Agents Finally Got Reliable in 2026 With New "Harness" Engineering
summary: The AI industry is shifting from asking 'can an agent do this?' to 'can we trust an agent to do this repeatedly, safely, and at scale?' Harness Engineering is the key.
details: The AI landscape has evolved rapidly. After focusing on prompts in 2023 and workflows in 2024, 2025 saw a push for better context management. Now, 2026 is defined by "Harness Engineering," which provides the code, constraints, and feedback loops necessary for AI agents to execute long-running tasks reliably.

A "harness" acts as the scaffolding around a raw LLM, providing the discipline needed to prevent errors and ensure consistent performance. This shift from prompt engineering to system engineering means builders are now effectively "harness builders."

Meta's new Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full models address critical agent pain points with "Active Memory" and "Active Focus" features, designed for professional, long-running tasks. The premium "Full" version is priced at $50/month, signaling these are serious productivity tools.

The cost of running AI agents at scale is also decreasing significantly. Models like MiniMax M3.1 Flash offer a 3x increase in inference speed while cutting costs by 70%, making advanced agentic tasks more accessible.
This "Great Unbundling" of AI cost from capability has demolished the barrier to entry for solo developers and small teams, enabling reliable, multi-step agents without massive budgets.

Beyond software, the next infrastructure challenge is power. The immense data centers required for large models are straining grids, leading to renewed interest in Small Language Models (SLMs) and on-device AI for energy and latency benefits.
Collaborations like Meta and Apple's work on the Muse Spark Open for local execution on Mac Studio highlight the trend towards privacy, energy efficiency, and reduced latency through on-device AI.

The AI hype cycle is maturing into a reliability cycle. Tools are becoming cheaper, memory is improving, and harnesses are strengthening, paving the way for developers to build more robust and dependable AI applications.
